haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Unknown email and wrong password get the same 401, same body and headers, "Invalid email or password". A dummy hash keeps timing equal.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 with Retry-After and "Too many attempts for this account". It records nothing, does not extend the lock, does not check the password, and rolls back.
haiku-low.q3: If the password matches, the session pointed to by the request's sid cookie is deleted, even if expired or unknown, and a new session is created.
haiku-low.q4: Only a random session ID, named sid. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it. It also has Path=/, Secure and SameSite=Lax.
haiku-low.q5: It stops 12 hours after login. The absolute limit is never extended, so continuous use past that point is rejected and the user is redirected to /login.
haiku-low.q6: It finds no matching unexpired row, replies 303 to /login, and clears the sid cookie.
haiku-low.q7: It deletes the sessions row matching the cookie's hash before replying. If the row is already gone or there is no cookie, it still replies 303 to /login and clears the cookie.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, shared by both instances. Any instance looks up the SHA-256 hash of the cookie there, so no sticky sessions are needed.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with email_key and failed_at. Failures are counted by failed_at within the last 10 minutes, using the database clock.
haiku-low.q10: It compares the hash of the cookie value to id_hash, and checks expires_at is later than now. On success it sets expires_at to the earlier of now plus 30 minutes or absolute_expires_at.
haiku-low.q11: Login page with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.", status 503, Retry-After: 30. The cookie is unchanged and no session is created.
haiku-low.q12: A cleanup job every 15 minutes on each instance deletes sessions whose expires_at is more than a day old, in batches. It is idempotent.

sonnet.q1: It does not differ. Both get the same 401 login page, "Invalid email or password", with identical body and headers. The dummy bcrypt hash makes timing equal.
sonnet.q2: It is locked (the 5th failure sets locked_until to now plus 15 min). A locked attempt gets 429 with Retry-After and "Too many attempts for this account". Nothing is recorded, the lock is not extended and the password is not checked.
sonnet.q3: On successful login the session that the sid cookie points to is deleted, even if it was expired or unknown. Then a new session with a new ID is created.
sonnet.q4: Only the random session ID (256-bit, base64url); no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: 12 hours after login. The absolute_expires_at is never extended, even though each request restarts the 30-minute idle clock.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns no row, so the server replies 303 to /login and clears the sid cookie.
sonnet.q7: If a sid cookie is present, the server deletes the sessions row whose id_hash matches before replying. If the row is already gone (or there is no cookie), it still replies 303 to /login and clears the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, keyed by the SHA-256 hash of the session ID. Any instance hashes the cookie's ID and queries the shared Postgres, so no sticky sessions are needed.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table (email_key, failed_at), indexed on (email_key, failed_at). The server counts rows for that email_key whose failed_at is within the last 10 minutes, using the database clock now().
sonnet.q10: It compares the hash of the cookie value to id_hash, and checks that expires_at is later than the database now(). If valid, it sets expires_at to the earlier of now plus 30 minutes and absolute_expires_at, and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A database error rolls back and creates no session. The browser gets the login page with "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Try again shortly.", status 503, Retry-After: 30, and its cookie is unchanged.
sonnet.q12: The cleanup job, which runs every 15 minutes on each instance. It deletes in batches the sessions rows whose expires_at is more than a day old.
